published.citation: Luque et al. 2024, dayside brightness temperature from the NIRSpec G395H white light of detector NRS2, 1360 +/- 100 K: 1360 +/- 100 K, https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.03411

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 4.5 µm (JWST NIRSpec) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: of the two detectors, the one with the smaller relative uncertainty and the longer wavelength, 3.8 to 5.2 µm
